audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer identified Twofold Hex as Aurora's escape and even labelled it '(Blink)'. Twofold Hex is her Q — a 9s missile that curses, with a recast that drags the curses back through anyone in the way. Her escape is Across the Veil (W): a leap that puts her in the spirit realm, invisible, with bonus move speed, on a 22s cooldown at rank 1. Tracking the wrong ability means the reader all-ins into a full escape.
audit.why: The whole page's commit rule ('all-in when it is down') was pointed at a 9s poke instead of a 22s escape, so the advised window was wrong by 13 seconds. The Weirding (E) is a separate, smaller disengage: damage and slow, then a backward hop.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0], dosFull[2].d, report[5].t and focus.text repointed at Across the Veil with the 22s; dontsFull[1].d now states what The Weirding actually does.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven level rows named a side their own 'why' contradicts: whys[0] says you out-poke a level-1 Aurora on a 'Skill' row; whys[1] literally opens "It's even" on a Kennen row; whys[2] and whys[3] describe her dodging every mark chain on Kennen/Skill rows; whys[5] says her first item out-pokes and out-bursts you on a Kennen row.
audit.why: Across the Veil coming online is what ends Kennen's window, and her first-item poke beats his HP bar; he only reclaims the game in teamfights. The packet levelChart matches that reading row for row.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Kennen / Skill / Aurora / Aurora / Skill / Aurora / Kennen in both layers, with phases[2], [3] and [5].why rewritten to state the real reason.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers, and no statement of the ultimate race.
audit.why: Across the Veil 22/21/20/19/18, Twofold Hex 9/8.5/8/7.5/7, The Weirding 15/14/13/12/11, Between Worlds 140/120/100. Kennen's Slicing Maelstrom is a flat 120 against her rank-1 140 — a 20s edge that is the reason his level-6 window exists at all.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rebuilt with the real numbers and the 120-vs-140 race; breakdown.mid and phases[3]/[5].why now carry them.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal anywhere on the page, despite Spirit Abjuration healing her off every spell and attack that damages you.
audit.why: Riot's text: her spells and attacks exorcise spirits from damaged enemies, and those spirits follow her and heal her. In a poke lane that sustain is what decides the extended trade.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now buys Oblivion Orb, and dontsFull[0].d states the passive by name.

notes: The full layer had Twofold Hex labelled '(Blink)' and treated as Aurora's escape; it is her 9s Q poke. Every commit rule on the page was therefore pointed at the wrong cooldown and repointed at Across the Veil (22s at rank 1). The content layer's shorthand is also loose — it repeatedly calls the blink 'E' and the exile 'W', when Across the Veil (W) is the leap-and-vanish and The Weirding (E) is the damage-slow-plus-backward-hop — but rewriting seven content strings on shorthand alone risked more churn than value, so only the level-chart rows were touched there and the naming issue is recorded here. Level chart flipped on five rows in matched pairs; both layers already agreed with each other and now agree with the packet and with every whys[N].
